summary.headline: MRPL Q2 FY27 standalone net profit of ₹1,881 crore on ₹3,210 crore EBITDA, nearly 3x year-ago, despite August shutdown and September CHTU fire.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone net profit was ₹1,881 crore on EBITDA of ₹3,210 crore, roughly three times the ₹639 crore of Q2 FY26, despite a planned August shutdown. Throughput was 4.18 MMT against a quarterly peak of about 4.5 MMT. H1 net profit rose to ₹2,796 crore from ₹2,367 crore, and borrowings fell by over ₹5,000 crore in six months to ₹9,245 crore. A fire at the Coker Hydrotreater Unit on 30 September 2026 led to a provisional ₹118.76 crore exceptional loss, with restoration targeted by mid-December. Management said the West Asia disruption is forcing reactionary crude sourcing, with higher freight ($7–9/bbl) and more Russian and spot barrels.

segments.name: Refining
segments.commentary: Q2 throughput 4.18 MMT against a ~4.5 MMT quarterly peak, after a planned August shutdown. Management guided Q3 total throughput close to Q2 levels, with a marginal product-mix hit from the CHTU fire (under 2 percentage points of distillates).

segments.name: Marketing (retail and direct)
segments.commentary: Retail volumes rose about 50% YoY as private OMCs curtailed sales; direct marketing grew 30–40% YoY. Diesel sales were about 40 TMT in Q2 vs 20 TMT in Q1. Solvents (xylol, MTO, toluene) nearly doubled YoY to about 10 TMT per month. Retail margin was marginally negative for H1; network has 257 outlets, targeting about 500 by FY28 end.

segments.name: Petrochemicals
segments.commentary: Polypropylene was cut in H1 to prioritise LPG supply. A new JV, OPML (ONGC 50%, OPaL 25%, MRPL 25%; MRPL investment ₹12.5 crore), was formed to market petrochemicals.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 throughput expected close to Q2 levels, with CHTU restoration targeted by mid-December 2026.
No refinery maintenance planned until the next cycle around April 2027.
FY27 capex guided at ₹1,200–1,500 crore (management cited ₹1,200–2,500 crore at one point), covering refinery maintenance, revamps, small IRR projects and retail; modest capex for about two years.
Grid power project expected online by FY-end, to bring fuel and loss further down from below 10% toward the 9.5% target.
Retail network target of about 500 outlets by end of FY28.
Company expects to maintain a strong balance sheet in the current year; balanced approach of debt reduction, modest capex and shareholder returns.
Net cracks cited at about $20/bbl above average landed cost (industry average); company will not publish quarterly GRM.

qa_highlights.question: How is MRPL managing freight costs and the all-in delivered cost of crude into November and December?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is widening procurement to West Africa and the Americas, adding STS operations and DAP cargoes; freight typically $7–9/bbl, and it declined to give an all-in DES cost figure.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth and capex plans given the strong balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex kept at ₹1,200–1,500 crore, mostly revamping and some retail, confined to about a couple of years; the Devanagonthi–Bengaluru ATF pipeline is the one major project.

qa_highlights.question: What were product-wise refinery output and marketing volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail volumes up about 50% YoY, direct marketing up 30–40%, diesel sales about 40 TMT in Q2 vs 20 TMT in Q1, solvents about 10 TMT per month; no petrol direct-marketing figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Will MRPL publish quarterly GRM, and what is sustainable refining margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No, quarterly GRM will not be published given methodology differences; net cracks cited at about $20/bbl above average landed cost, with SAED moving in line with international markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a government cap on GRM around $15/bbl?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the landed price and cracks drive the final numbers and that the range is around the figure cited, but did not address any cap directly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q3 impact of the CHTU fire on distillate yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 total throughput not expected to change significantly; product mix marginally impacted, with less than a couple of percentage points of distillates at risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crude sourcing mix and Russian share?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East about 20–21%, domestic about 25%, Russian about 30–32% of Q2 basket, with the remainder from other sources including West Africa and the Americas.

qa_highlights.question: Is the shift to DAP crude cargoes temporary or structural for term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East sellers have offered DAP, STS and a tender for the first time; it expects some form of these variations to persist, while continuing to insist on DAP to de-risk until things stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the energy consumption and fuel and loss outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel and loss brought below 10% by cutting steam use and losses; grid power expected fully available by FY-end, with the 9.5% target to follow.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at ₹1,200–1,500 crore (management restated ₹1,200 crore to ₹1,500 crore on Q&A; opening remarks said ₹1,200 crore to ₹1,500 crore), covering refinery maintenance, revamping, small IRR projects and retail
Capex beyond FY27 kept in a modest range for about a couple of years; management declined to give forward growth guidance
Devanagonthi to Bengaluru airport ATF pipeline authorised by PNGRB; expected completion by FY2029-30 at a cost of ₹200 crore plus
Grid power project expected to be fully available by financial year end, seen driving fuel and loss below 10% toward 9.5% target
CHTU reconstruction under way after 30 September 2026 fire; restoration targeted by mid-December 2026; no refinery maintenance until around April 2027
Retail network at 257 outlets across Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh; target about 500 outlets by end FY28
demand_pricing: Retail sales up about 50% YoY in Q2 as private OMCs curtailed retail operations; management called it not structural but expects some stickiness
Direct marketing up 30–40% YoY, with supply to other OMCs described as market-building; diesel sales about 40 TMT in Q2 vs 20 TMT in Q1
Solvents (xylol, MTO, toluene) up nearly 100% YoY to about 10 TMT per month; other products flat YoY as product basket is fixed

Most domestic sales at RTP level; net cracks about $20/bbl above average landed cost (industry average, not MRPL-specific); analyst-cited implied GRM about $14.86–14.9/bbl, which management did not confirm
Freight rose to roughly $7–8/bbl average, up to $9 typical and $10 in extreme cases; management declined to give an all-in DES cost
Crude mix Q2: domestic about 25%, term about 20%, spot the balance; Russian about 32% vs about 28% in Q1; Middle East about 20–21%
Exports limited to a couple of cargoes in H1 (about 15% of volume on quantity basis, as stated); exports expected low in coming months
RLNG intake curtailed on high spot offer prices; swing between diesel and ATF possible within a month depending on crude
risks_watch: CHTU restoration slipping beyond mid-December 2026, which would keep product mix constrained and affect Q3 throughput near Q2 levels
Freight and crude availability: freight $7–9/bbl with reactionary sourcing; Middle East term cargo curtailment via the Strait of Hormuz
Retail and direct-marketing volume gains may reverse once private OMCs normalise; management says retail margin was marginally negative for H1
Possible government cap on GRM near $15/bbl, which management did not directly address
Grid power timing for fuel and loss improvement (target 9.5%); exceptional loss of ₹118.76 crore is provisional and subject to insurance and final assessment

We are targeting a retail presence of about 500 retail outlets by the end of FY 2028.
We continue to follow a balanced portfolio approach of debt reduction, modest capex and shareholder returns.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the financial result and balance sheet but cautious and reactionary on crude sourcing, freight and margins. Management deflected on GRM publication, the government cap question and forward-looking growth, and repeatedly said figures are preliminary or "anybody's guess".

adds.what: Retail network expansion to about 500 outlets by end FY28 (from 257 today)
Devanagonthi to Bengaluru airport ATF pipeline (authorised by PNGRB)
Grid power project to cut fuel and loss toward 9.5% (efficiency, not capacity)

growth.why: Management guided Q3 throughput close to Q2's 4.18 MMT (vs ~4.5 MMT peak), with CHTU restoration by mid-December and no refinery maintenance until ~April 2027, but gave no explicit revenue growth figure and declined forward growth guidance beyond FY27 capex of ₹1,200–1,500 crore and the 500-outlet retail target by FY28; EBITDA growth was derived from the brief (₹3,210 cr vs ₹639 cr profit) and not

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA of ₹3,210 cr against ₹639 cr PAT a year ago and net cracks about $20/bbl above landed cost, but freight of $7-9/bbl, reactionary crude sourcing and the CHTU fire (under 2pp distillate hit) cap how much of this carries forward.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Throughput is 4.18 MMT vs a ~4.5 MMT quarterly peak, but no new refinery capacity is guided; the only items are a 257-to-500 retail outlet build by FY28 and the ₹200 cr+ Devanagonthi-Bengaluru ATF pipeline due FY2029-30.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q3 throughput guided close to Q2's 4.18 MMT, and retail volumes are up ~50% YoY and direct marketing 30-40% YoY, but management calls the retail surge not structural and export volumes are expected low.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is held at ₹1,200-1,500 cr and management guides modest capex for about two years, with no new large project beyond the already-authorised ATF pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 net profit rose to ₹2,796 cr from ₹2,367 cr and the balance sheet is strengthening, but management gave no explicit revenue or margin guidance and called figures preliminary.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CHTU restoration slipping past mid-December would constrain distillate mix, and freight at $7-10/bbl plus Middle East crude curtailment via Hormuz are live risks; a possible GRM cap near $15/bbl was not addressed.

rows.label: Debt reduction continues
rows.why: Borrowings fell over ₹5,000 cr in six months to ₹9,245 cr and D/E dropped to 0.55 from 1.01, with management prioritising debt reduction alongside modest capex and shareholder returns.

rows.label: Grid power to cut fuel and loss to 9.5%
rows.why: Fuel and loss is 9.86% in H1 FY27 (vs ~11% earlier), and grid power is expected fully available by FY-end to push it toward the 9.5% target.

rows.label: Crude sourcing diversification and exports
rows.why: Management is widening procurement to West Africa and the Americas with STS and DAP cargoes, but exports were only a couple of cargoes in H1 (about 15% of volume) and are expected low.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 result, balance sheet and debt paydown, but cautious on crude freight, reactionary sourcing and margins, and deflected on GRM publication, the possible $15/bbl cap and forward growth.
